items.stem: A sari-sari store hands over a bottle of soda and receives 20 pesos. Looking at the part where the goods go out, which choice names the resource, the event and the agents?

options.text: Resource: the soda. Event: the sale. Agents: the owner and the customer.
options.feedback: The resource is the thing of value, the event records that it changed hands, and the agents are the people on each side.

options.text: Resource: the owner. Event: the soda. Agents: the 20 pesos.
options.feedback: These roles are mixed up. People are agents, and the thing of value is the resource.

options.text: Resource: the sale. Event: the soda. Agents: the customer.
options.feedback: The sale is the event, because it records something that happened. The soda is what changed hands.

options.text: Resource: the 20 pesos. Event: the soda. Agents: the owner only.
options.feedback: The 20 pesos are the resource in the payment half of the pair. In the goods half the resource is the soda, and both people are agents.

items.stem: Maria pays ₱18,000 in one transfer for three subjects. Juan pays the ₱7,500 for one subject in two installments. Why does the model need a separate allocations table that links payments and enrollments?

options.text: One payment can cover many enrollments, and one enrollment can have many payments.
options.feedback: A pairing that is many-to-many needs its own table, and the amount applied to each enrollment can be stored only there.

options.text: Banking rules require payments to be kept in a table of their own.
options.feedback: The reason comes from the shape of the data, not from banking rules.

options.text: A separate table makes the payments table faster to search and back up.
options.feedback: Speed is not the reason. Without the allocations table you could not store installments or shared transfers at all.

options.text: Each enrollment should always have exactly one payment, so the table is optional.
options.feedback: That holds only until the first student pays in installments or one transfer covers several subjects.

items.stem: A school records each enrollment and each payment as separate events. Which question needs both kinds of event to answer?

options.text: Which students hold a seat and have not paid?
options.feedback: This question looks for a gap between two events that should pair up, an enrollment with no matching payment.

options.text: How many seats does ITENT 45 have in total?
options.feedback: This needs only the resource, the seats. No event is involved.

options.text: Which room is ITENT 45 held in this term?
options.feedback: This is a fact about the course and its room. It needs no payment.

options.text: What is Maria's student number on record?
options.feedback: This is an attribute of one student and needs neither event.
